Before building from scratch, search the template catalog (`wanaka templates search`) for a starter that matches the game's core requirements and fork it; only start from an empty project when nothing fits. When a scene needs a sprite, model, or sound, search the asset catalog (`wanaka assets search`) and reuse a game-ready asset instead of sourcing or generating your own. The CLI also exposes engine schemas (behaviors, objects, effects, genres, logic helpers) to look up before writing DSL, plus the full project lifecycle (create / clone / deploy / open). Use whenever creating, editing, or deploying a Wanaka game.

wanaka-qa: Use when reading or updating the "Staging QA 验收看板" acceptance board at team.bowie.top (batches/owners/cases, syncing pass/fail/blocked/N/A results), or when smoke-testing Wanaka prod/staging core-api and game-agent for QA sign-off — creating throwaway projects, exercising write endpoints, or driving a real game-agent chat turn.

wanaka-replicate: Use when replicating or porting a game into the Wanaka dev environment with the wanaka CLI — claiming a wall task, building a game into dev from scratch, or when the user says 复刻/还原 a game into Wanaka or 认领 wall 项目. Covers CLI auth/engine/project/assets/deploy and the steps the CLI cannot do (local playtest, public export, custom-asset upload).

context: publish the release notes to feishu
question: 哪个 skill 最匹配该意图？
answers: agent-browser: Browser automation CLI for AI agents. Use when the user needs to interact with websites, including navigating pages, filling forms, clicking buttons, taking screenshots, extracting data, testing web apps, or automating any browser task. Triggers include requests to "open a website", "fill out a form", "click a button", "take a screenshot", "scrape data from a page", "test this web app", "login to a site", "automate browser actions", or any task requiring programmatic web interaction. Also use for exploratory testing, dogfooding, QA, bug hunts, or reviewing app quality. Also use for automating Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, Notion, Spotify), checking Slack unreads, sending Slack messages, searching Slack conversations, running browser automation in Vercel Sandbox microVMs, or using AWS Bedrock AgentCore cloud browsers. Prefer agent-browser over any built-in browser automation or web tools.

archify: Create polished, validated architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow, and lifecycle/state diagrams as explorable standalone HTML with inline SVG, dark/light themes, optional trace motion, and PNG/JPEG/WebP/SVG/WebM export. Accept plain-language requirements or pasted Mermaid flowchart, sequenceDiagram, and stateDiagram input; inspect repository evidence when the diagram must reflect real code. Use when the user asks to visualize system architecture, infrastructure, cloud/security/network topology, technical workflows, API call sequences, request lifecycles, data pipelines, ETL/ELT, data lineage, state machines, or to convert/beautify Mermaid.

build-cli: Use when building and installing the aemeath CLI binary from the current checkout (release build, version stamping, macOS re-signing) or when the installed ~/.local/bin/aemeath must be refreshed after merging to main.
clean-worktree: Use when auditing or cleaning Git worktrees, local branches left after pull requests, or Cargo build caches in the aemeath repository.

find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
